title: Make Array Empty
summary: Given an array of distinct integers, repeatedly remove the smallest element or move the first element to the end until the array is empty.
statement: Given an array of distinct integers, repeatedly remove the smallest element or move the first element to the end until the array is empty. Return the count of operations performed.
constraints: Repeatedly remove the first value when it is currently smallest; otherwise move that first value to the end.
Return the total number of removals and moves until the array is empty.
hints: Remove values in increasing numeric order; only rotations determine the cost between removals.
A Fenwick tree stores which original indices remain alive.
Count live indices from the current position through the target, wrapping at n when necessary; remove the target and continue after it.
Original circular order among survivors never changes, so each counted live index corresponds to exactly one move or final removal.
editorial: Original circular order among survivors never changes, so each counted live index corresponds to exactly one move or final removal.

One and two are removed immediately, then four rotates behind three before both are removed, for five operations.
